killed.claim: "Wrong curve for the job… Applied between the two stops of a symmetric loop it produces an asymmetric tick (slow-out on the way down, snap on the way back), not a breath." (challenge-D-design.md:422-426)
killed.refutation: FALSE — a misreading of CSS animation timing semantics. `animation-timing-function` is applied PER KEYFRAME INTERVAL, not once across the whole iteration. /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/status/ApiOfflineChip.vue:82-85 declares two equal-length intervals (0%→50%, 50%→100%) and :88 applies `var(--ease-standard)` to BOTH. cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) is itself an accelerate-then-decelerate curve, so each half starts slow, speeds through the middle and settles slow — the composite is symmetric, with a soft hold at each extreme. That is a breath, and it is precisely what the file asks for. There is no "snap on the way back".

killed.claim: 'There is no truncate, no max-w-, and the API applies no name-length cap (api/src/modules/admin/service/tags.ts:45-70 inserts `name` unvalidated for length)' -- evidenced by a measured 67-character tag rendering a 462px, two-line, 55.9/68.8/88.4px-tall lozenge.
killed.refutation: FALSE, and it is the vivid centre of D-10's evidence. The cap exists one layer above the cited one: api/src/modules/admin/schema.ts:27-34 defines `createTagBody = z.object({ name: z.string().min(1).max(30).regex(/^[a-z0-9-]+$/, "must be lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens"), category: z.string().min(1).max(30) })`, and api/src/modules/admin/routes/tags.ts:21-24 runs `createTagBody.safeParse(await c.req.json())` and throws ValidationError BEFORE calling the service. The service is indeed unvalidated -- because its only caller already validated. A 67-character tag, and any tag containing an uppercase letter, space or punctuation, cannot exist in this product. The lozenge was injected by the seat's own DOM replica, so the measurement describes an input the system rejects. RESIDUAL, stated fairly: 30 chars of Fira Code still wraps at 320px, so the mechanism survives at roughly half the claimed magnitude; the 'no cap' claim does not.

killed.claim: 'Duplicate create produces a duplicate pill and a duplicate v-for key' -- measured `tagNames: ["moody","moody","cool","warm"]` -- plus 'the load path preserves server order (warm, cool) while create re-sorts, so creating one tag silently reorders every other tag on screen.'
killed.refutation: REFUTED against the real backend on both limbs. (1) api/src/platform/db/db.ts:98 creates `db.collection("tags").createIndex({ name: 1 }, { unique: true })`, and api/src/modules/admin/service/tags.ts createTag catches Mongo `code === 11000` and throws `ConflictError("Tag already exists")`. So a re-create returns 409, never '200 with the existing row' -- the shape C-7 calls 'the ordinary idempotent-POST shape' is one this API cannot emit. The measured duplicate came from a Playwright route.fulfill mock. (2) The order limb dies the same way: TagRepository.findAllSorted() is `this.col.find().sort({ name: 1 })`, so the load path is already name-ascending, matching the create path's localeCompare in the restricted [a-z0-9-] alphabet. The `warm, cool` server order was likewise mock-supplied. What actually happens on duplicate create is a 409 -> ApiProblem -> `catch { console.warn }` -> nothing, which is C-5, already charged. RESIDUAL: two independent ordering policies maintained in two places (useAdminTags.ts:75-77 vs the server sort) is a real latent duplication -- at MINOR, not MAJOR, and with no visible symptom.

killed.claim: 'Contrast the sibling console: AdminUsersPanel.vue:289-300 gates *every* destructive admin action behind a Glass-7 ConfirmDialog with an explicit "This cannot be undone."'

D-1's softer phrasing ('ships a full glass-ui Dialog confirmation ... for its destructive verbs', challenge-D-design.md:118-122) survives; C-4's 'every' does not, and it matters because C-4 leans on it to argue the omission is deliberate rather than merely uneven. The core charge -- tag delete has no confirmation while the sibling has one for its user-level verbs -- stands.

killed.claim: 'the port's published contract advertises a writable cell that throws "Write operation failed: computed value is readonly" at runtime.'

killed.claim: 'The comment at :49-50 asserts "the ONE loading-ink register"; there are two, and only one is named.'

What is doubled is the SHAPE (row silhouette vs chip silhouette) -- which L-15's own next paragraph concedes is 'a legitimate second shape'. The surviving limb, that the chip shape has no module home and therefore cannot be reused or kept in step, is correct and unaffected.

missed.claim: `surface="glass"` and `variant="breath"` on `<Skeleton>` are INERT fallthrough attributes -- glass-ui 7.0.0's Skeleton accepts exactly one prop. A silent glass-7 adoption regression that vue-tsc structurally cannot catch, and that all three axes quoted verbatim without seeing.
missed.proof: AdminTagsPanel.vue:57-64 renders `<Skeleton v-for="i in 5" :key="i" surface="glass" variant="breath" class="h-7 rounded-full" :class="..." />` (the two props are on :60 and :61). node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/skeleton/Skeleton.vue.d.ts declares the complete prop surface as `type __VLS_Props = { class?: HTMLAttributes["class"] }` -- nothing else. Both props therefore fall through onto the rendered DOM element as literal `surface="glass" variant="breath"` attributes and are read by no code. Vue treats undeclared attributes as legal fallthrough, so the demo typechecks green forever. Same defect at AdminListSkeleton.vue:13,15,16,18. THE CORPUS ALREADY HOLDS THE PROOF: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md rows M-12 and M-14 adjudicate exactly this claim TRUE against the same .d.ts, for AdminListSkeleton -- so the finding was available and none of AdminTagsPanel's three seats applied it. Two second-order consequences: (a) AdminTagsPanel.vue:49-50's comment asserts a deliberate register ('the ONE loading-ink register') that is only half-real -- the ink comes from .skeleton-ink-register, the two props contribute nothing; (b) the standing owner bracket at docs/tranches/T/audit/w8-certification/passes/admin.p1.md row A-1 asks the owner to choose between `variant="breath"` and `variant="shimmer"` on this exact line -- a question that cannot be answered, because neither value is read. Glass 7.0.0 was adopted whole at W44; the props presumably existed in 5.x and died silently.

missed.claim: The create path violates the server's published input contract on the most ordinary input a human will type, and the violation is completely invisible. `toLowerCase()` is mistaken for validation.
missed.proof: useAdminTags.ts:70-74 sends `newName.value.trim().toLowerCase()` and `newCategory.value.trim().toLowerCase()`. The server's contract is api/src/modules/admin/schema.ts:28-32: `name: z.string().min(1).max(30).regex(/^[a-z0-9-]+$/, "must be lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens")`, enforced at api/src/modules/admin/routes/tags.ts:21-24. `toLowerCase()` removes case; it does not remove spaces, underscores, periods, slashes or accents, and it does not enforce max(30). So typing 'Deep Blue' -- the single most likely first input for a tag taxonomy -- sends 'deep blue', the server returns 400 ValidationError, client.ts:153 throws ApiProblem, and useAdminTags.ts:80-82 swallows it into `console.warn`. Net user-visible result: the button was enabled (AdminTagsPanel.vue:42 tests only non-emptiness and `creating`), the click did nothing, the inputs did not clear, the list did not change, no message appeared. There is no `pattern`, no `maxlength`, no client-side validation, and no error cell anywhere in the component. C-5 and D-8 charge 'mutations fail silently' generically and reach for 409/403/429/network-drop as examples; neither identifies the trigger that a real admin hits on attempt one. This is the component's most reachable failure and the corpus does not name it.

missed.claim: `useTagEdit.loadAllTags`'s `force` parameter is dead code -- the one mechanism that could reconcile L-3's two tag caches is published on the port and never invoked.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/useTagEdit.ts:21 declares `loadAllTags: (force?: boolean) => Promise<void>` on the exported UseTagEdit interface; :34 implements `async function loadAllTags(force = false)` with the short-circuit at :35 (`if (loaded.value && !force) return;`) and a second at :36-39. `grep -rn loadAllTags demo/` returns exactly three call sites and all three pass nothing: BrowsePane.vue:223 `pm.tagEdit.loadAllTags();`, TagEditPopover.vue:81 and :85 `tagEdit.loadAllTags();`. So the parameter has never been exercised, and useAdminTags's create/delete have no path to invalidate the sibling cache even if someone wanted one. L-3 cited the short-circuit at :35 but read `force` as an available escape hatch, which is what let it file the staleness as an unexecuted hypothesis; it is in fact static fact plus a dead parameter.

missed.claim: The create row is a form with no form semantics and no keyboard submit: Enter does nothing in either field, and the in-repo idiom for exactly this exists two directories away.

There is no `<form>`, no `@submit`, no `@keydown.enter` and no `@keyup.enter` anywhere in the file. Pressing Enter after typing a tag name is a no-op, so the only way to create a tag is to reach for a 28x36 icon-only button. The repo already owns the idiom: `grep -rn 'keyup.enter|@keydown.enter' demo/` -> CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:132 (`@keydown.enter="saveCurrentPalette"`), SearchFilterBar.vue:95 (`@keydown.enter="applyColorSearch"`), ImageDropZone.vue:22. missed.claim: The producer rung that `h-7` is trying to reach already ships as `size="xs"` -- so C-12/D-11's prescribed cure invents a rung that exists.
missed.proof: D-11 (challenge-D-design.md:518-521) prescribes: 'if the admin toolbar genuinely needs a tighter rung than sm, that rung belongs in glass-ui as a size value; the six consumer sites then carry a prop, not a class.' It already does. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:5 declares `ButtonSize = Extract<Size, "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg">`, and the token is `--control-h-xs: max(calc(1.75rem * var(--ui-scale)), var(--control-floor))` -- 1.75rem is 28px, i.e. precisely `h-7`, with the coarse-pointer floor preserved for touch. The correct edit at AdminTagsPanel.vue:10 and :40 (and the four sibling sites) is `size="xs"` plus deleting `h-7 px-2`: one token, zero producer work, and the touch floor stops being silently discarded by a hardcoded 28px. A cure that proposes producer work already done is a cure that will not be taken.

missed.claim: Both e2e specs justify their defensive selectors with a shell behaviour the shell deleted -- stale rationale that makes vacuous gates look considered.
missed.proof: e2e/smoke/admin/flows/tag-create.spec.ts:30-32 and tag-delete.spec.ts:33-38 both explain `.filter({ visible: true })` with 'The Tags panel mounts in both layout slots (the off-breakpoint copy is display:none)'. demo/color-picker/App.vue:61-70 records the opposite as a named invariant: 'X6: single-mount by breakpoint. D3-01's overflow figures (+9.6 px Chromium / +10.7 px WebKit). Everything downstream of a *populated* wall remains bounded by the corpus's own standing caveat (L5-6 / pass-4 §C): no capture in this programme has photographed the Browse wall against real production rows on the audited configuration, so every wall-state figure in the corpus comes from a route stub or a proxy whose row shapes were hand-authored. Whether the empty-invitation CTA (D5-04) has a meaningful destination on the desktop two-pane arm, where `My Palettes` is already co-visible. That is a design ruling, not a measurement, and it decides whether the cure is `<template #emptyAction>` or a copy change.

killed.id: D-5 — "the track override is an owner-edict-5 violation that defeats the spectrum variant"
killed.claim: `--slider-track-bg: var(--ink-muted, …)` is a per-instance override of a design-system root that defeats the `variant="spectrum"` the same component requests, and the cure is to delete it.
killed.refutation: Three-way refutation against the served bytes. (1) `--slider-track-bg` is the PRODUCER'S OWN PUBLISHED SEAM, not an override: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.css declares `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-track{height:calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem)*1.5);background:var(--slider-track-bg,var(--secondary))}` — a custom-property handoff with a fallback, i.e. exactly the pattern D's own sibling axis exonerates (challenge-L-library.md:448-451: "The `--slider-track-bg` feed on line 202 is *correct* by contrast"). Four other demo sites already use it (ExtractControls.vue:32,75; GenerateControls.vue:305; ComponentSliders.vue:197). (2) The transparent `.slider-range` is the PRODUCER'S RECIPE, not something the demo defeats: glass-ui.css `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-range{-webkit-backdrop-filter:none;box-shadow:none;background:0 0}`, restated deliberately at demo/styles/foundation.css:559-574 with the minification bug that forced the restatement. (3) The prescribed cure would REGRESS A LANDED, GATED ACCESSIBILITY FIX: demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:190-201 records that the default `var(--secondary)` track computed ~1.09:1 light / 1.26:1 dark on the well (WCAG 1.4.11 wants ≥3:1), and e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:1161-1175 is the born-RED gate asserting the config track ≥3:1 with `--ink-muted` STAMPED. Deleting the rule (D's cure §8) turns that spec RED. What survives is a design judgment only — a flat achromatic value fed into a hook shaped for a gradient — not an edict violation and not a deletable rule.

killed.id: D-7 — "the live readout violates the NORMATIVE card-lock law on both required mechanisms"
killed.claim: BlobPane's 31 readouts lack `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` and lack `ch` worst-case reservation, both required by demo/DESIGN.md's NORMATIVE card-lock law.
killed.refutation: Four refutations. (1) The quotation is truncated: demo/DESIGN.md:63-65 reads "Two mechanisms, both required wherever live numeric values render **at display scale**" — D-7 drops "at display scale"; the readout is `text-micro` (11 px), the opposite of display scale. (2) The law's normative TEST is card-rect stability — DESIGN.md:60-62: "a value change may never move the card: dragging any component slider from min to max changes NO containing card rect (±0px)". A readout re-flow inside a fixed-width flex row in a `w-full h-full` Card (ConfigSliderPane.vue:98-101) does not move the Card. D-7 measures the wrong object. (3) MECHANISM 2 WAS FORMALLY RETIRED by this tranche: demo/picker/display/ColorComponentDisplay/readoutReservation.ts:1-19 — "The retired mechanism — every cell reserving its worst-case `ch` as `min-width` — rendered the worst case as BLANK width on every non-worst value (39–51% of every cell was empty reservation) … the goal survives, the mechanism dies — no per-cell `ch` reservation returns." Charging a component for lacking a mechanism the tranche deleted, and prescribing its return (D's cure §7), is a regression request. (4) Mechanism 1 is satisfied by the FACE: DESIGN.md:70-72 "Fira Code is tabular by default; Fraunces is NOT"; the readout is `font-mono` → `var(--font-stack-mono)` (Fira Code). A computed `font-variant-numeric: normal` on a monospaced face does not prove non-tabular rendering. RESIDUAL (real, MINOR): `fmt` at ConfigSliderPane.vue:84-86 swings the readout between kinds (`Number.isInteger(v) ? String(v) : v.toFixed(3)`), so Tempo reads "1.950" → "2" → "2.050" — a formatter-consistency defect that tabularity would not fix and that belongs on SliderDef as a `precision` field.

killed.id: D-13 — "the promise is awaited and discarded, so a rejected clipboard write is an unhandled rejection"
killed.claim: copyAsJson's discarded await leaves an unhandled rejection with no user-visible result.
killed.refutation: `writeClipboard` cannot reject. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/useClipboard-D36OTaeT.js:3-16: `if (typeof navigator > "u" || !navigator.clipboard?.writeText) return { ok: !1, reason: "no-api" }; try { return await navigator.clipboard.writeText(e), { ok: !0 } } catch (e) { return console.warn(…), { ok: !1, reason: "clipboard-api" } }` — every path returns a result object. There is no unhandled rejection, ever. The sibling axis states this correctly (challenge-C-implementation.md:344-346: "never throws"). The real defect is narrower and is confirmed separately: a discarded RESULT, not a swallowed rejection.

killed.id: L-1 / BPC-1 — the prescribed cure ("adopt the producer's `BLOB_HERO` preset")
killed.claim: HeroBlob should stop hand-patching four keys and select the shipped `BLOB_HERO` preset; the demo maintains a divergent inline hero register.
killed.refutation: The defect is confirmed; the CURE is structurally unsound as written and would silently revert two landed, owner-ruled fixes. Measured diff of the installed 7.0.0 constants (node --input-type=module over @mkbabb/glass-ui/blob-config): BLOB_HERO differs from BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS in EXACTLY five leaves — `geometry.satelliteCount 3→4`, `geometry.satelliteRadius 0.082→0.1`, `geometry.orbitRadius 0.17→0.3`, `geometry.eccentricity 0.05→0.04`, `membrane.smoothK 0.05→0.06`. It does NOT carry `bodyRadius 0.325` (it is 0.22) and does NOT carry `fissionAmp 0.6` (it is 0). So selecting BLOB_HERO would (a) break the W29 rendered-diameter contract — `2 * bodyRadius ≈ 0.65` — which test/picker-blob-config.test.ts:26-31 pins by regex, turning vitest RED; and (b) revert the WR-2/T-49c "never-meatball" fission arming documented at HeroBlob.vue:134-150 back to the shipped `fissionAmp: 0` ("the whole fission branch was DEAD at the hero"). Both axes assert the producer/demo divergence without checking which side of it is load-bearing. The correct shape is a DEMO-side preset table seeded from the current hero register, not adoption of the producer's.

killed.id: D-6 — the attribution ("the cause is the costume from D-5")

killed.refutation: The attribution inverts cause and scope. Under forced colors the track is substituted whether it resolves `--ink-muted` or the producer default `var(--secondary)` — neither is in the roster at demo/styles/foundation.css:685-696, which lists `.gradient-rail, .rail-handle, .readout-rail, .swatch-row > *, .generate-swatch, .shadow-swatch, .goo-blob-canvas, .watercolor-swatch, .glass-slider[data-variant="spectrum"] .slider-range, [data-color-surface]` and NOT `.slider-track`. The finding is real but is neither caused by nor confined to BlobPane — see the missed finding on the inert roster entry, which is the correct, wider statement.

killed.id: BPC-1 headline — "nine of ten sliders do not reach the render" (and D-3's "five of six")
killed.claim: Nine of ten sampled sliders, and five of six max-range sweeps, produce zero pixels — i.e. essentially the whole console is disconnected from the shader.
killed.refutation: Over-claimed, and contradicted by the corpus's own measurements. Only FOUR atoms are structurally inert (the geometry literals — confirmed separately by arithmetic). For the rest, the three axes disagree with each other on the same atoms: D-3 phase 2 records `Core Glow 0.06→1` at **4.91% of the canvas WHILE PARKED** (challenge-D-design.md:176) whereas BPC-probe11 records the same atom at **7 px of 32761 (0.02%)** (challenge-C-implementation.md:34); and D's own probe 7 (challenge-D-design.md:195-196), which wakes the renderer first, shows `Noise Amp` at 2.34× and `Iridescence` at 1.90× the live jitter — i.e. non-geometry atoms DO reach the render once the loop is awake. That is the expected structural behaviour: HeroBlob.vue:152-178 spreads `...appBlobConfig.surface` and `...appBlobConfig.color` INTO the computed, so writes to those atoms invalidate `heroConfig` and the producer re-reads `t.config` per frame (`c = () => t.config ?? a ?? s`, dist/blob.js). The correct decomposition is: 4 sliders structurally inert (BLOCKER) + the remainder unobservable while parked (BLOCKER, separately confirmed) — not "nine dead controls".

killed.id: D-1 — cure #1 applied alone (`blob: { left: "blob", right: null }`)
killed.claim: Give Blob a route, not a sidecar — the exact shape `atmosphere` already has one entry above it. "Kills D-1 outright."
killed.refutation: In isolation it makes the route strictly worse: the ONLY `<Blob>` in the application lives inside the Picker pane (demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:13; `grep -rn "<Blob" demo` returns that one hit). Setting `right: null` and `left: "blob"` removes the Picker — and with it the app's only rendered blob — from `/#/blob`, leaving a 31-slider form tuning nothing at all. The step is only coherent as part of D's package (cure #2 supplies a stage), and D does not flag the ordering hazard. The one-line, order-independent fix for the stated mechanism is `defaultPaneIndex: 1` on viewSchema.ts:179, exactly as the sibling axis proposes.

missed.claim: The app's forced-colors protection roster is INERT for every spectrum slider: it exempts an element the producer paints transparent, while the element that actually carries the colour is absent from the list. This is app-wide and includes the Picker's four chromatic channel ramps — not a BlobPane-local issue as D-6 framed it.
missed.proof: demo/styles/foundation.css:685-696 enrols `.glass-slider[data-variant="spectrum"] .slider-range` in the tier-1 `forced-color-adjust: none` roster. But that element has no paint: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.css declares `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-range{-webkit-backdrop-filter:none;box-shadow:none;background:0 0}` — transparent by recipe — and demo/styles/foundation.css:559-574 restates the producer's own intent for that same selector, so the repo already knows it. Consequence: under WHCM every spectrum slider in the app loses its track colour, including the Picker's Lab channel ramps fed at demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:192-197 via `--slider-track-bg`, and the exemption that exists to preserve colour-display surfaces protects nothing anywhere. Cure is one selector in the roster, at the root — not the deletion of a consumer's contrast cure.

missed.claim: BlobPane's load-bearing justification comment points at the wrong module: it attributes the paletteStops writer to App.vue, which contains no such watch.

missed.claim: HeroBlob has `onActivated` but no `onDeactivated`, and its wake watchers stay live while the picker pane is KeepAlive-deactivated — so a colour change made from a route that does not show the Picker resumes a ~7 ms/frame WebGL2 loop for a subtree that is not painted.
missed.proof: demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:120-127 wraps every pane in `<KeepAlive :max="max">`; Vue does not suspend watchers on deactivate, only lifecycle hooks. demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:246-250 registers `onActivated` and demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:227-230 registers `onScopeDispose` (unmount only) — there is no `onDeactivated`. The `cssColorOpaque` watch at :264-280 therefore still calls `noteBlobActivity()` (:267), which sets `blobPaused.value = false` (:217) and re-arms a 5.3 s live window. Routes whose left pane is not `color-picker` — `atmosphere`, `gradient`, `extract`, `generate`, `about`, `admin-*` per demo/shell/viewSchema.ts — deactivate the picker while remaining able to change the colour model. The file's own comment at :233-236 asserts "navigating away parks the blob", and :181-183 states the cost the gate exists to avoid ("~7ms EVERY frame it is mounted, even fully idle — 54fps vs the blob-off 85fps").

missed.claim: The reset hazard is already cured on the sibling consumer by shaping the DEFAULTS OBJECT rather than the reset function — proving the repo knew the shallow-`Object.assign` semantics and that the real root is reset living in the wrong module, not merely an unlucky merge depth.
missed.proof: demo/scenes/atmosphere/aurora-atoms.ts:15-20: "The demo's initial atmosphere SHAPE — the one source App.vue seeds the reactive atoms with AND AuroraPane's 'Reset' restores to. **Carries NO `seed`**: the seed is the live picker colour (App.vue's watch), so Reset restores the shape … without disturbing the colour." That is a function invariant encoded in a data literal, and it is why ConfigSliderPane.vue:92-94 is safe for AuroraPane and unsafe for BlobPane — BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS is the PRODUCER's constant and does carry `color.paletteStops` (verified in the emitted 7.0.0 defaults). BlobPane structurally cannot use the aurora cure. Neither axis noticed the precedent, which both sharpens L-3's severity and rules out its 'deep per-atom merge' half-cure: the atom the pane does not own is producer-declared, so ownership, not merge depth, is the fix.

missed.claim: Dead branch inside the 33-line type guard: the outer `readonly unknown[]` arm can never be taken.
missed.proof: demo/scenes/blob/BlobPane.vue:39-40 — `: BlobConfig[A] extends readonly unknown[] ? never`. No top-level member of `BlobConfig` is an array: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/blob/types.d.ts declares `geometry|satellites|membrane|color|surface|interaction` (objects), `morphT: number` and `tempo: number` (caught by the first arm), and `quality: BlobQuality` (a string union). superlatives: THE GENERATED SELF-ALIAS SET — genuinely excellent and I re-derived it independently. `vite.config.ts:38-49` *generates* the value.js alias map from `package.json#exports` with anchored regexes, so a specifier the demo can write is one a real npm consumer can write; an alias cannot drift from the export map nor prefix-match into a subpath. Census confirms it holds today: `grep -rho '@mkbabb/value.js/[a-z]*' demo/` → color 25, css 10, math 6, easing 5, quantize 4 — five of seven published subpaths and NOTHING unpublished; `grep -rn 'from "@mkbabb/value.js"' demo/` → zero bare-root imports; zero `@src/` or `../../src/` reaches. Five L passes all found this and all said keep it verbatim through any restructure. They are right.

THE BARREL DISCIPLINE IS REAL WHERE IT IS PRACTISED. `demo/palettes/browser/card/index.ts:1-3` and `search/index.ts:1-2` are named-re-export-only with the tree-shake rationale written down ("a Vue SFC's scoped `<style>` is a side-effecting import; named re-exports let the bundler tree-shake unused members per consumer"). And it is honoured in fact: `grep -rn 'from "[^"]*browser/[^"]*\.vue"' demo/` → empty. The tree complies with a boundary whose ESLint guard has been inert since W43 (L-4/N-2) — which is a compliment to the authors and an indictment of the guard.

THE CAPTURED-ETAG ORDERING IN `TagEditPopover`. `TagEditPopover.vue:73-77` reads the row out of `pm.remotePalettes` and derives `paletteETag(source)` BEFORE the optimistic `emit("update:tags", updated)` mutates it — with the reason in the comment ("the ETag reads `currentHash`/`updatedAt`, which the tag edit hasn't bumped yet"). That is a two-tab lost-update window closed deliberately, in the one component of this blast radius that is otherwise unreachable. C pass 3 credits it; I re-derived it and agree.

THE TYPED-STATE DISCIPLINE IN `availability.ts`. `:167-172` `markApiUnreachable()` opens with `if (apiAvailability.value === "misconfigured") return;` under the comment "A designed misconfig is NOT an unreachable backend — never mislabel it," and `:119-130` builds a 400-character actionable message naming the origin, the base URL and the fix. The transport layer diagnoses correctly, refuses to downgrade its own diagnosis, and hands the pane four distinguishable species. Every failure in the C-1/L-11 family is downstream of a layer that did its job.

EMIT/BINDING CORRESPONDENCE IS EXACT. I checked all fifteen: `PaletteCard.vue:200-218` declares `click, delete, publish, save, vote, rename, editColor, addColor, feature, adminDelete, setVisibility, fork, versions, flag, editTags, export`; `BrowsePane.vue:102-116` binds fifteen of the sixteen (`publish` belongs to PalettesPane). killed.claim: "In dark mode the pill's background is pixel-identical to the card behind it ... CR 1.00 ... The 12%-destructive wash composites to nothing. There is no chip" (challenge-D-design.md:88-100, :351-356).
killed.refutation: FALSE by re-measurement of the seat's OWN evidence file. In `evidence/desktop-1440-dark-misconfigured.png` I sampled the modal colour above, to the right of, and below the chip: uniformly (66,55,47). The chip fill is (86,57,50). CR = 1.114, not 1.00 -- and the fill is measurably warmer/lighter, i.e. the destructive wash DOES composite (+20 levels of red). killed.claim: "the live region flaps every 30 s ... each transition unmounts/remounts a `role="status"` node -- twice ... Screen-reader users get the same sentence announced twice, every half minute, indefinitely" (challenge-D-design.md:338-347).
killed.refutation: FALSE on two independent grounds, both decidable from source. (1) NOTHING POLLS. `assertApiAttemptAllowed()` is reached only from `fetchWithRateLimitRetry` (`demo/platform/transport/client.ts:74`), which runs only when a surface issues a request. There is no `setInterval`, no timer, no watcher anywhere in `availability.ts` or `client.ts` that re-probes on the cooldown. An idle offline session issues zero probes. (2) EVEN A FAILED PROBE CANNOT RE-RENDER. `markApiUnreachable()` (`availability.ts:167-172`) executes `apiAvailability.value = "unavailable"` -- assigning the value the ref already holds. Vue's `ref` setter is `hasChanged`-guarded (Object.is), so no reactive effect is triggered, the `computed`s do not re-evaluate, and the `v-if` node is never unmounted. There is no oscillation, no remount, and no re-announcement. D-7(a) (no recovery arm) is unaffected and is confirmed separately.

killed.claim: "`--ease-standard` ... applied between the two stops of a symmetric loop produces an asymmetric tick (slow-out on the way down, snap on the way back), not a breath" (challenge-D-design.md:421-426).
killed.refutation: FALSE. CSS `animation-timing-function` is applied independently to EACH keyframe interval, not once across the cycle. The keyframes are `0%,100% { opacity: 1 } 50% { opacity: 0.35 }` (`ApiOfflineChip.vue:82-85`), so interval 0->50% and interval 50->100% each get `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` mapped onto their own progress. The down-phase and the up-phase are temporally identical by construction; velocity is zero at both stops. The pulse IS symmetric, and it does hold briefly at each extreme -- which is exactly the 'breath' character the finding claims is absent. (`--ease-standard` -> `--motion-ease-standard: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)`, verified at glass-ui `dist/styles/tokens/scheme-spring.css:1` via the `bridges.css` `@theme inline` alias.)

killed.claim: "`VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md` Section 6 holds the same line for ambient motion (\"terminates within five seconds or exposes one persistent keyboard-operable still/pause control\")" -- tabulated as a canon FAIL at challenge-D-design.md:516.

The clause at `docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:145` reads in full: "Continuous **Aurora/Blob ambient** motion terminates within five seconds or exposes one persistent keyboard-operable still/pause control whose state is announced and remembered." It is scoped by name to the Aurora/Blob ambient field -- the surrounding bullets at :13 and :15 are all about that same subject -- and does not reach a component-level status glyph. The canon FAIL row is not supported by the text it cites. (The WCAG 2.2.2 argument may stand on its own merits; the tranche-canon claim does not. Note also that motion-quarantine.md:119 M-28 rules a structurally similar "blinks forever" claim FALSE, though for a different component and on PRM grounds.)

killed.claim: "glass-ui exposes a full duration ladder (`--duration-instant/fast/normal/slow/panel/xl/xxl` ...). None is consumed. Owner edict 6 wants animations moved or tokenized" (challenge-D-design.md:418-421).

The nearest shimmer rungs are `--duration-shimmer-fast: 3s` and `--duration-shimmer: 5s`. "Consume the existing ladder" therefore necessarily changes the motion's tempo -- the finding neither says so nor picks a rung. Tokenizing here requires MINTING a token in the producer, which is a different (and larger) instruction than the one written.

C-3 and D-6 both found the gate but framed the lamp as a co-present second seat ("the component is not in the DOM at all, while the dock lamp is", challenge-C-implementation.md:179-181), which is only true under `npm run dev`. This is the strongest available form of the PR-08 finding and no axis states it.

"public" : "private" }}`). Cure: both surfaces must read one `degraded` predicate over the union, not each spell their own.

missed.claim: The K-INV5 small-caps annotation register has FIVE hand-rolled seats, three of them inline `style=` attributes -- a direct owner-edict-5 violation the two-seat framing hides.

missed.claim: The mono voice on which the component's entire "instrument register" identity rests is never webfont-loaded, so its typography is a local-install lottery and its small-caps are UA-synthesised.
missed.proof: `--font-stack-mono: "Fira Code", "Fira Code Fallback", "Fira Mono", monospace` (`node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/scheme-motion.css:1`), bridged to `--font-mono` (`bridges.css`) and consumed by `.fira-code` (`demo/styles/utils.css:10`, applied at `ApiOfflineChip.vue:14,22`). But the only `@font-face` rules in the whole application are the five Fraunces faces inlined at `demo/color-picker/index.html:47-88`; `find demo -name '*.woff2'` returns Fraunces only, and glass-ui's compiled `dist/glass-ui.css` declares ZERO `@font-face`. On any machine without Fira Code locally installed the chip falls back to the platform generic `monospace`. Compounding it: `font-variant: small-caps` (`:45`) requires an `smcp` feature the font must ship; absent it the UA synthesises small caps by scaling capitals, which at an 11px em gives roughly an 8px effective cap height -- under `letter-spacing: 0.06em` and 72%-opacity ink. That is the real legibility mechanism behind the "faint" reading D-1.3 attributes to opacity alone, and it undermines the reproducibility of every screenshot-derived contrast number in the corpus (all captured on a machine where the font resolved). Repo-wide rather than chip-local, but load-bearing for this component's claims.

missed.claim: The `misconfigured` alert is present at first render rather than inserted as a change, so the loud register is the one screen readers never announce -- while the quiet register is the one they do.
missed.proof: `demo/platform/transport/client.ts:43` calls `initApiEnvironment(BASE_URL)` at module-evaluation time, which sets `apiAvailability.value = "misconfigured"` (`availability.ts:161`) BEFORE the Vue app mounts. For a returning user `savedColorStrings.length > 0` is already true at first paint, so `ApiOfflineChip.vue:11-18` renders its `role="alert"` region WITH its content in the initial tree. ARIA live regions announce changes to a region already in the accessibility tree; a region that exists with content at page load is generally not announced. The `unavailable` face is the opposite: the latch trips on the first fetch rejection (`client.ts:80-83`), i.e. after mount, so THAT insertion is a genuine change. Net effect: the register designed to be assertive and attention-owning is silent to AT, and the register designed to be quiet is the audible one. C's negative-proof section raises the mounted-with-content concern honestly as a hypothesis (challenge-C-implementation.md:433-440) but does not notice that `initApiEnvironment`'s module-eval timing makes it a certainty for the alert branch specifically -- and L-9 verifies that same timing fact without connecting it to the a11y consequence.

missed.proof: `demo/styles/utils.css:90-98` `.dashed-well { display: flex; flex-direction: column; ...; border: 1.5px dashed var(--card-edge); }` -- the well's own edge is `--card-edge`. `ApiOfflineChip.vue:51` then draws `border: 1px solid var(--card-edge)` INSIDE that well, on a fill measured 1.131:1 (light) / 1.114:1 (dark) above it. So the chip's only remaining separation from its ground is a thinner stroke of the identical ink the ground already uses to describe itself. D-8's cure ("pick a real tier from the producer's ladder") is directionally right but misses the actual rule being broken: an annotation inside a well must not restate the well's own edge token. Also confirms that `.self-start` (`CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:116`) is `align-self` in a column flex container, so the chip is content-width -- relevant to C-4/D-10's overflow arithmetic, which neither seat grounded in the real container.

All three claim completeness on a diff that is not complete. Benign in practice -- a flex item's automatic minimum size clamps shrinkage at the specified 0.4rem -- but it is exactly the silent drift L-2 predicts forks produce, found in the very table meant to prove the fork.

superlatives: EXEMPLARY (motion): the reduced-motion idiom is the best form of it in the tree. `ApiOfflineChip.vue:81-90` places BOTH the `@keyframes offline-dot-pulse` block AND the `animation:` declaration inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, so under `reduce` no animation exists at all -- rather than the common `animation: none` counter-patch that then has to out-specify two global `!important` neutralisers (`demo/styles/animations.css:184-193` and glass-ui `dist/styles/utilities/a11y-overrides.css:1`, both enumerated in codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md sections 1). The tranche's own keyframes census lists this block among the conforming ones (excavation/DESIGN-CANON-BRIEF.md:88, per challenge-L-library.md:359-361). All three axes credit it independently and all three are right.

EXEMPLARY (motion cost): the animated property is `opacity` and nothing else, on a 6.4px element -- compositor-only, no layout, no paint, no `will-change` needed. Zero forced-reflow properties appear anywhere in the file's 51 lines of CSS. For a status glyph that may run for an entire session this is the correct budget.

EXEMPLARY (architecture): the DI seam. `ApiOfflineChip.vue:31,35` reads the latch through `useApiClient()` -- a provide/inject key with a fail-fast missing-provider guard (`demo/platform/transport/useApiClient.ts:54-61`) -- rather than importing the `apiAvailability` module singleton. L-library.md:404-406 calls it "the one structural decision in the file that is right"; I would go further. It is why C could drive the full four-state render matrix against the app's own module records at all, and it is why every cure in this corpus is a ~10-line change rather than a rewrite. It should survive every remediation untouched.

EXEMPLARY (state discipline): self-gating is total and honest. `unknown` and `available` render literally nothing -- no empty shell, no zero-height node, no skeleton, no placeholder (`:12`, `:20`). Two `computed`s over a four-member union with no default arm to get wrong, no props, no emits, no lifecycle, no listeners, no timers. The component has no cleanup surface, therefore no leak class and no unmount race.

EXEMPLARY (upstream engineering): the `misconfigured != unavailable` distinction at the latch is genuinely good work and should not be lost in the cull. `demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:20-35` documents the precise failure mode -- the browser collapsing a CORS refusal and a network-down into one bare fetch rejection, so a loopback dev page aimed at the cross-origin prod API MISLABELS its own misconfiguration as "backend offline". `markApiUnreachable:169` refuses to relabel a misconfig; `assertApiAttemptAllowed:189-191` throws a different typed error synchronously; `devMisconfigMessage:119-130` names the page origin, the resolved base URL and the exact fix. Every seat's cure correctly preserves the latch and kills only the surfaces. That is the right call.

EXEMPLARY (audit craft, CHALLENGE-L): the attribution proof at challenge-L-library.md:76-79 is the model of the genre. It settles the owner's OM-5 question on two numbers read off the live cascade -- `pad: 4.8px 8.8px` = `0.3rem 0.55rem` = `DockStatusLamp.vue:56` against the chip's `0.3rem 0.7rem`, plus `position: absolute` against in-flow `inline-flex` -- and then refuses the easy conclusion: "the answer is a trap, because *both* render it." It answers the question that was asked, correctly, and then answers the question that should have been asked.

EXEMPLARY (audit craft, CHALLENGE-C): the negative-proof discipline at challenge-C-implementation.md:396-440. Each bullet is a live hypothesis from the brief's hazard list, checked and killed with the reason -- and the one genuinely open a11y concern (live regions mounted together with their content) is labelled a hypothesis, given the exact experiment that would settle it, and NOT banked. That restraint turns out to be the correct read of the very defect D-7(b) got wrong by asserting a mechanism it had not traced. The probe-hygiene ledger (section 5) records `localStorage` restored byte-exactly and the probe host removed, verified.

VERIFIED EXACT (measurement integrity): challenge-L-library.md:135-146's footprint reproduces to the line -- `wc -l` on the six files gives 91 + 7 + 123 + 65 + 160 + 85 = 531. Likewise challenge-D-design.md:66-77's PIL sampling of OM-5 reproduces to three significant figures under my own independent implementation (fill (225,144,140), ink (201,57,48), CR 2.084), and challenge-D-design.md:104-110's light-chip numbers reproduce within antialiasing noise (fill (243,239,235), well (233,225,217), CR 1.131). In a corpus where I refuted several claims, the arithmetic that was shown was overwhelmingly sound; the failures were in scope, citation and inference, not in measurement -- with the two exceptions recorded in killed K5 and K13.

killed.claim: "The re-entering vnode carries the same `key="error"` as the vnode still leaving. The pending enter is dropped and nothing is ever mounted." (challenge-C-implementation.md:69-82)
killed.refutation: REFUTED against Vue 3.5.35's actual runtime. Two separate guards make the same-key-during-leave case recoverable: (a) `BaseTransition` sets `leavingHooks.afterLeave = () => { state.isLeaving = false; instance.job() }`, so the leave's completion always re-renders the pending child; (b) `resolveTransitionHooks`'s `enter` reads `leavingVNodesCache[key]` and force-completes a same-key leave via `leavingVNode.el._leaveCb()` precisely so a fast toggle cannot wedge. The 200 ms `--duration-fast` window is therefore not the cause, and the same-key collision is the one case Vue explicitly handles. The real cause is unrelated to keys or timing — see MISSED item 1. The report's own decisive datum ("survives SPA navigation, only a hard reload restores it") is not predicted by a keying collision at all, but is predicted exactly by the latched `isLeaving` flag.

missed.claim: The real mechanism behind C-1, proven statically and fixable in one line: EmptyState's template-root HTML comment makes it a dev-mode multi-root Fragment, and Vue 3.5.35 never fires `afterLeave` for such a fragment — so any `<Transition>` hosting it latches `isLeaving = true` forever.
missed.proof: demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:2-13 is a comment node at template root, *before* the `v-if` div at :14. Compiling the live SFC with @vue/compiler-sfc: `comments: true` → `_createElementBlock(_Fragment, null, [ _createCommentVNode(...), ... ], 2112 /* STABLE_FRAGMENT, DEV_ROOT_FRAGMENT */)`; `comments: false` → a single-root `div`. node_modules/@vue/runtime-core/dist/runtime-core.esm-bundler.js, `const remove = (vnode) => { const { type, el, anchor, transition } = vnode; if (type === Fragment) { if (DEV && vnode.patchFlag & 2048 && transition && !transition.persisted) { vnode.children.forEach(child => child.type === Comment ? hostRemove(child.el) : remove(child)) } ... return } ... const performRemove = () => { hostRemove(el); if (transition && ... ) transition.afterLeave() } }`. `setTransitionHooks` attaches the hooks to the **Fragment**, never to its children, so the recursed `remove(child)` runs `performRemove()` with `transition === undefined` — `afterLeave()` is never called, `BaseTransition.state.isLeaving` never resets, and every subsequent render returns the empty placeholder. This predicts every symptom challenge-C measured and could not explain: permanent blank, no self-heal, survives SPA nav (the Transition instance in BrowsePane persists), hard reload only, and — decisively — why *only* the error branch kills the pane: BrowsePane.vue:40's three direct children are a plain `div` (:43), EmptyState (:61, the only Fragment), and PaletteCardGrid (:80, single-root because its comment is correctly placed inside at :7-11). Blast radius: 35 demo components compile to DEV_ROOT_FRAGMENT; three sit as direct `<Transition>` children — EmptyState (BrowsePane.vue:40/61), PaletteCardSkeleton (ExtractWorkbench.vue:102-107), MixResultDisplay (MixPane.vue:111-118). Cure: move the comment inside the root element. demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11 already states this rule verbatim — "a leading comment node would make this a multi-root component" — and is the only file in the tree that knows it.

The single best piece of type design in the cone: it turns a runtime convention into a compiler-checked fact, and it is what let me refute one of my own candidate findings (a silent no-op on a remote-palette collision) in thirty seconds.

The K-PALID id-honesty work, demo/palettes/types.ts:15-27 — `id?: string` with a nine-line comment explaining that the server is slug-identified and emits no id, so 'declaring it string was a type-lie that let a client-minted local key masquerade as a persisted server id.' demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:112-116 — detectDevMisconfig is pure, total, three lines of policy, separately exported for testing, and carries the inline proof '// never fires in prod'. killed.id: D-5 points 1/2/3 — the edict-5 and "fallback as material" charge
killed.claim: "A per-instance custom-property override that defeats the variant the same line requests" — owner edict 5 violation; and "the fallback taken as the default", the config console pinning the else-branch forever.
killed.refutation: Both halves fail against the live tree. (a) --slider-track-bg is the PRODUCER's declared hook, not a per-instance override: glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.css — .glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-track{background:var(--slider-track-bg,var(--secondary))} — and it is the app's uniform idiom at four sites: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:195-203 (the picker's own Lab ramps), demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:32,75, demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:305, demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:202. The sibling axis says so explicitly and is right: challenge-L-library.md:449-451 — "The --slider-track-bg feed on line 202 is *correct* by contrast: a custom-property handoff, not a selector reach." Nothing per-instance is overridden and nothing is defeated: the transparent .slider-range is the producer's spectrum recipe (background:0 0) for every consumer in the app. (b) The --ink-muted track is not a fallback taken by accident — it is a RULED, GATED WCAG 1.4.11 cure. ConfigSliderPane.vue:190-201 records the born-RED measurement (spectrum track computed var(--secondary), ~1.09:1 light / 1.26:1 dark on the well), and e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:1160-1212 is the live gate asserting .config-console .configurator-row .slider-track >= GRAPHICS_FLOOR against the well ground. Charging the discharge of a contrast finding as a design error, without engaging the floor it discharges, is a false defect. Only the value-signal consequence survives, re-listed under confirmed.

killed.id: D-7 — "violates the NORMATIVE card-lock law on both required mechanisms"
killed.claim: The live readout breaches demo/DESIGN.md's NORMATIVE card-lock law, quoted as "Two mechanisms, both required wherever live numeric values render".
killed.refutation: The charge is manufactured by truncating the quote. demo/DESIGN.md:59-62 reads: "Two mechanisms, both required wherever live numeric values render **at display scale**" — the challenge's block quote (challenge-D-design.md:351-355) drops "at display scale", converting a display-ramp law (its own opening sentence is "Hero/readout numbers may be as audacious as the display ramp allows") into a universal one so that an 11px text-micro token falls inside it. Nor is the law's actual prohibition shown to be broken: DESIGN.md:57-59 defines it as "a value change may never move the card … changes NO containing card rect (+/-0px)", and the readout sits in ConfiguratorRow's <div class="flex items-baseline justify-between gap-3"> opposite a truncate label in a min-w-0 column (compiled configurator-M5OaIlJd.js), so a width swing re-flows only that row's internal split — no card rect moves, and D supplies no card-rect measurement. The residual — fmt's Number.isInteger branch (ConfigSliderPane.vue:84-86) flipping the readout between 1 and 5 characters mid-drag, and the absence of tabular-nums where glass-ui ships a .tabular-nums utility — is a real MINOR readability defect, not a NORMATIVE breach, and does not carry MAJOR.

killed.id: BPC-6 — "31 sub-24px targets; WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 has no pointer-type exemption"
killed.claim: The 12x24 thumbs fail SC 2.5.8, and the @media (pointer: coarse) gate at ConfigSliderPane.vue:218-230 is therefore the wrong cure.
killed.refutation: SC 2.5.8 (Target Size Minimum, AA) has an explicit Spacing exception: undersized targets conform if a 24-CSS-px-diameter circle centred on each does not intersect another target or another undersized target's circle. Each config row holds exactly ONE target — ConfigSliderPane.vue:137-143 passes no canReset, so ConfiguratorRow emits no reset button — and rows are >=48px apart centre-to-centre: .configurator-row stacks a text-small label line (--type-small = 16.4px at 1440 at --type-leading-body), gap-1.5 (6px), the spectrum track at calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem)*1.5) = 24px and py-1 (8px), inside a section wrapper carrying a further gap-1.5. 24px circles 48px apart do not intersect, so the exception is satisfied and there is no SC failure to charge. The measurement (w=12 h=24, all 31 rows) is correct; the conformance conclusion is not, and "this pane IS the app's tap-target outlier" is a density observation about 31 sliders on one route. The L sibling reached the calibrated verdict on the same numbers (challenge-L-library.md:602-606).

killed.id: BPC-1 mechanism 2 — "Propagation: the snapshot objects are the second root"
killed.claim: "geometry/surface/color are re-spread into plain snapshot objects inside the computed, while membrane, satellites and interaction pass through as the live reactive proxy. The one slider that works (membrane.smoothK) is on the proxy side."
killed.refutation: A spread inside a computed is not a propagation barrier. HeroBlob.vue:152-178 is computed<BlobConfig>; { ...appBlobConfig.geometry } invokes the reactive proxy's ownKeys and get traps, registering a dependency on every enumerated key, so ANY slider write to surface.*, color.* or the two non-overridden geometry.* keys invalidates the computed and hands <Blob> a fresh object — exactly the "wake-repaint shape" HeroBlob.vue:63-66 says the producer built for. The snapshot atoms are therefore as live as the proxy atoms; only the six literal assignments (bodyRadius, orbitRadius, satelliteRadius, eccentricity, fissionAmp, paletteStops) are inert by construction. C's own sibling axis measured Iridescence — a surface, snapshot-side atom — moving 6.86% above noise in the live window (challenge-D-design.md:196), contradicting the snapshot theory from inside the corpus. The nine nulls in the BPC-probe11 table are explained by BPC-2's idle park, which that probe's protocol did not defeat.

killed.id: L-12 — "a global stylesheet owned by a leaf component"
killed.claim: .pane-scroll-fade is defined in an unscoped <style> inside PaneHeader.vue and "belongs in demo/styles/, per the standing rule that global keyframes and global classes live there."
killed.refutation: The standing rule says the opposite, and names this exact class as the landed cure. demo/DESIGN.md:388: "**No new global utility class for one consumer** — colocate to the component's <style scoped> (post-D.W4 Lane A: `.pane-scroll-fade`, the touch-gate cluster, `.palette-tab-content`, `.palette-card-grid` moved out of style.css)", corroborated by demo/styles/foundation.css:577-579 which records the same move. PaneHeader.vue:43-53 documents why the block must be unscoped (nine sibling pane roots consume it) and why it lives there (PaneHeader owns the only consumers of --pane-scroll, the named scroll-timeline the block defines). L-12 charges a documented, executed decision as a defect and cites the very rule that was written to justify it.

killed.id: D-1 / D-2 severity framing — BLOCKER x3
killed.claim: "Nine defects rise to BLOCKER/MAJOR"; D-1 (mobile non-mount), D-2 (no preview) and D-3 (no causal link) are all BLOCKERs.
killed.refutation: Only D-3 earns BLOCKER. D-1 is a missing one-key schema default (defaultPaneIndex: 1 at viewSchema.ts:179-188, exactly as viewSchema.ts:122/:150 already set it) and the pane is one tap away on the dock's segmented control — C's MAJOR is the calibrated grade. D-2's cited law is a tranche-V TARGET, not a shipped contract: docs/tranches/V/PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:1-6 states "This is a product audit, not a new gate … W19-W29 execute their owned rows", and PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:54 books this precise family as PR-10 "Primary W28; executor W29" — an owned, un-executed remediation row; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:214's "dedicated Blob workbench" describes a composition that has never been built. Charging un-executed tranche-V build orders as BLOCKER defects of the pre-execution tree inflates the register and buries the one finding (D-3a) that is provable by arithmetic.

killed.id: D-6 mechanism — "BlobPane wears the attribute without the content and is protected in exactly the wrong place"
killed.claim: "The WHCM policy was written for a real spectrum rail; BlobPane wears data-variant=spectrum without the content and is protected in exactly the wrong place."
killed.refutation: The observable outcome is right; the attribution is wrong and the blast radius is far larger. .glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-range is transparent for EVERY spectrum slider in the app by producer recipe (glass-ui.css, background:0 0), and no demo site paints it — grep for slider-range in demo/ returns only the two foundation.css rules (:571, :693) and one comment. So foundation.css:693 does not protect "a real spectrum rail" anywhere; it protects an element that is always empty, for every consumer. BlobPane did not wear the attribute without the content — the roster was mis-targeted from the day it was written, and the picker is the bigger casualty. See missed defect M1 for the finding that actually follows.

missed.claim: The forced-colors tier-1 roster protects the one element no consumer paints and strips the ones they all do — so under WHCM the PICKER's four spectral Lab ramps are substituted away, destroying exactly the colour content the two-tier policy exists to preserve.

confirmed.claim: Off-idiom props declaration: `withDefaults` in a tree of reactive-props destructure, and `?: T | undefined` cancels `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`.

killed.claim: Negative proof N-4: "`tsconfig.base.json:11` sets `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`, so the explicit `| undefined` on all six optional props is CORRECT, not noise. No finding."
killed.refutation: Backwards, and it would entrench the weaker type. `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` exists precisely to make `?: T` and `?: T | undefined` DIFFERENT: with the flag on, `?: T` forbids an explicit `undefined` assignment while `?: T | undefined` re-admits it. So EmptyState.vue:74-88's unions do not satisfy the flag — they opt this component's entire prop surface out of it. The near-twin proves the alternative compiles in the same program: demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:46-51 declares `message?: string; retryLabel?: string` with no unions under the same tsconfig. challenge-L-library.md:326-350 (N-7) states this correctly; D's N-4 and L's N-7 are in direct contradiction and D is the wrong one.

killed.claim: "Cure (architectural, not a patch): give EmptyState a STABLE ROOT that never unmounts, and swap only the interior on `variant`, with the action slot in a persistent footer outside the swap. Then neither the announcement region nor the retry control is a casualty of the retry."
killed.refutation: The prescribed cure cannot fix the defect it is prescribed for, and it contradicts the same report's own negative proof. (1) demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:41's `<Transition mode="out-in">` wraps the ENTIRE three-branch chain, and Retry sets `browsing.value = true` (demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:65-67), which flips to the `key="developing"` skeleton branch at :44-53. The whole `<EmptyState>` COMPONENT is unmounted by the host at that moment; the shape of its internal root is irrelevant. A stable root inside a component the parent destroys stabilises nothing. (2) The cure requires one root serving both species, but challenge-C-implementation.md:349-355 (N-4) proves in the same document that a single root with a mutated `role` goes silent to AT — and one stable root cannot be both `role="alert"` and `role="status"`. The real cure is at the host: do not flip to the loading branch while an error plate is displayed (or drop `mode="out-in"` for a keyed swap that tolerates same-key re-entry). Filing it against the leaf atom sends the repair to the wrong file.

killed.claim: `color: var(--ink-muted, var(--muted-foreground))` is "a second path that CAN ONLY EVER hide a boot-writer failure."
killed.refutation: The fallback has a documented, non-masking job. demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:106-108 states it verbatim for the identical rule: "Falls back to `--muted-foreground` before the boot writer runs" — it is the pre-hydration paint value, not a failure mask, because demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphereBoot.ts:100-106 stamps `--ink-muted` from a component watcher and nothing declares it in CSS (`grep -rn -- "--ink-muted\s*:" demo/` over CSS returns zero). The genuine defect is the OTHER one L-N-3 measures: the fallback value itself (`--neutral-5` = `hsl(30 22% 40%)`) is below the small-text floor on the plate, so the pre-boot register is the failing one. That is carried as confirmed under L-N-3, whose cure (declare `--ink-muted` statically in foundation.css beside `--accent-live` at :231, then delete the fallback) is sound. C-11's rationale is not.

killed.claim: "`justify-center` is a PROVABLE no-op" on both roots.
killed.refutation: Inert in fact today, but not provable in general — and the counterexample is in the corpus. `justify-center` on a `flex-col` becomes live the moment the box is taller than its content, and EmptyState's root is attribute-fallthrough-open: any host may pass a height. Its own near-twin does exactly that — demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:18 carries `flex flex-col items-center justify-center … h-full w-full min-h-0` on the same class recipe, where the centring is load-bearing. The correct claim is narrower: no CURRENT EmptyState host passes a height (verified — PaletteCardGrid.vue:23 passes only `col-span-full`; the ten admin/mix/browse sites pass none), so it is inert at all 16 call sites today.

(PalettesPane.vue:80), "Publish one from My Palettes and start the wall." (BrowsePane.vue:86), "Save two or more palettes, then pour them together here." (MixSourceSelector.vue:242) — the last two being cross-pane instructions with no control. missed.claim: `PaletteCardGrid`'s `role="list"` never owns a `listitem` in ANY state — the populated children are `role="article"` — so C-3's a11y break is unconditional and its cure is aimed at the wrong node.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:3 declares `role="list"`; its `<slot />` at :12 receives `<PaletteCard>` children whose root is `role="article"` (demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:22, with the comment at :2 saying so). ARIA 1.2 `list` → required owned elements `listitem`. So the container resolves to a list of zero items in the POPULATED state too, not merely at empty — challenge-C-implementation.md:131-151 scopes the violation to the empty case and prescribes changing EmptyState ("render a plain div", "accept the role as a prop"), which would leave the shipped default state just as broken. The canon also removes the pretext: docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:186 requires "no listbox/option fiction surrounds the field" and PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:78 rule 12 pins the card as "a bounded entity article". The correct repair is to drop `role="list"` from the grid, which closes C-3 without touching the atom's 16 call sites.

missed.claim: The Retry control is rendered INSIDE the `role="alert"` region, so its accessible name is swallowed into the atomic announcement and the assertive region owns a focusable descendant.
missed.proof: demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:14-27: `role="alert"` on the root, `<slot name="action" />` at :26 inside it; demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:67-75 renders a `<Button>` into that slot, and six admin sites do the same. `role="alert"` carries implicit `aria-atomic="true"`, so the whole subtree is announced as one string — challenge-C-implementation.md:161 measured exactly that and printed it ("The commons is unreachable. Failed to load palettes Retry") without noticing that the trailing word is the button's label being read as prose. 'alert' : 'status'"` — which would patch the role attribute in place and make the species change SILENT to assistive tech. superlatives: THE STRIP TRUTH FUNCTION'S DESIGN. `demo/scenes/atmosphere/aurora-harmony-stops.ts` is 40 lines, pure, dependency-light and colocated with its single consumer; it states its own law in its header (:6-8), explains WHY a raw `deriveAurora` preview would lie (:9-11), and computes each harmony row's preview by running the REAL calibrated resolve at the LIVE seed rather than showing a canned swatch (:34-40). The referent drifted (C-2) — the idea did not. This is the correct shape of a preview affordance and most codebases never get near it.

THE SEED BOUNDARY IS GUARDED BY AN ACTUAL PROBE, NOT BY HOPE. `useAtmosphere.ts:122-127` names the failure class in prose (a thrown getter dead-faults the reactive effect — the inv-N-1 white-screen class), then :141-146 and :365-376 both call `deriveAurora(css)` purely to see whether it throws BEFORE writing `auroraAtoms.seed`. The result is a deep-watched getter that is throw-free by construction, with the last-good value preserved on a transient. Two sites, one law, written down.

THE RESET CONTRACT. `DEFAULT_AURORA_ATOMS` (aurora-atoms.ts:53-71) deliberately carries NO `seed`, so Reset restores the atmosphere's SHAPE without disturbing the picker's colour — and both consumers `structuredClone` it (useAtmosphere.ts:128, ConfigSliderPane.vue:93), so the module-level constant can never be aliased or mutated by a running app. The rationale is written at :16-20. A genuinely well-reasoned default object.

ONE SERIALIZATION FOR CHIP AND ORACLE. `sample.ts:88-91`'s `stampStops` is the single `data-stops` encoder, consumed by `PreviewStrip.vue:24,44` for the DOM stamp and available to the test; and the strip itself is `aria-hidden="true"` (PreviewStrip.vue:39) so a decorative preview can never pollute an option's accessible name or typeahead. The a11y instinct and the test-handle instinct are both right, in a 60-line component.

REST-FREE BY ARCHITECTURE. `SelectContent` genuinely unmounts when closed, so the six-candidate resolve at AuroraPane.vue:129-134 costs nothing at rest — the claim at AuroraPane.vue:36-38 is architecturally true, not aspirational. (Only the open-state cost is unexamined; see missed.)

confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED, and D-design's negative proof #2 wrongly cleared it. ColorNutritionLabel.vue:208 `contrastInkFor(nodeFill.value) ?? ""` — an empty `color:` is dropped by Vue, so :122-126 emits backgroundColor without color, exactly what the comment at :118-120 swears never happens. ink.ts:158-174 returns null when neither neutral endpoint survives `safeAccentColor` unmoved. I recomputed C-2's measured ratio by hand and it is exact: fill rgb(213,0,211) relative luminance 0.18854, ink rgb(28,25,23) luminance 0.010049 -> (0.23854/0.060049) = 3.972 vs the reported 3.97. killed.claim: Duplicate create produces a duplicate pill and a duplicate v-for key; and the load path preserves server order while create re-sorts with localeCompare, so 'creating one tag silently reorders every other tag on screen'.
killed.refutation: BOTH LIMBS REFUTED against the shipped API. (a) The server does not return the existing row on a re-create — api/src/modules/admin/service/tags.ts:57-65 catches Mongo duplicate-key `code === 11000` and throws `new ConflictError("Tag already exists")`. adminRequest then throws ApiProblem at demo/platform/transport/client.ts:152-153, createTagAction's catch at useAdminTags.ts:80-82 fires, and NOTHING is appended. The 'ordinary idempotent-POST shape' the finding assumes is not this server's shape; the measured duplicate came from C's own page.route mock returning 200 with the existing row (challenge-C-implementation.md:267-272). (b) The load path does NOT preserve arbitrary server order — api/src/modules/admin/routes/tags.ts:13 is commented 'GET /admin/tags — list all tags, sorted by name' and api/src/modules/color/repository/tag.ts:12 is `this.col.find().sort({ name: 1 }).toArray()`. Since api/src/modules/admin/schema.ts:32 constrains names to /^[a-z0-9-]+$/, byte order and localeCompare agree over the entire admissible alphabet. Load and create cannot disagree. The underlying append-without-reconcile at useAdminTags.ts:75 remains a latent robustness weakness, but the filed defect is unreachable. (challenge-C-implementation.md:257-280)

killed.claim: 'the API applies no name-length cap (api/src/modules/admin/service/tags.ts:45-70 inserts name unvalidated for length)' — evidenced by a 67-character tag rendering as a 462 px two-line lozenge.
killed.refutation: FLATLY FALSE. The cap exists and is enforced before the service is called. api/src/modules/admin/schema.ts:27-34: `createTagBody = z.object({ name: z.string().min(1).max(30).regex(/^[a-z0-9-]+$/, "must be lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens"), category: z.string().min(1).max(30) })`, applied at api/src/modules/admin/routes/tags.ts:21-24 (safeParse → throw new ValidationError) before createTag(...) at :25. Thirty characters is the ceiling and there is no other tag-insert path in the tree. The 67-character tag that produced the 462 px lozenge, the 55.9/68.8/88.4 px wrap heights and the 'row's optical rhythm collapses' argument is a synthetic replica input the product cannot produce (D discloses the injection at challenge-D-design.md:29-34). The no-filter/no-pagination/no-ordering limb survives on its own evidence and is confirmed separately; this evidence block does not. (challenge-D-design.md:471-498, esp. :481-486)

killed.claim: 'the producer Chip remove button carries the producer's own target geometry (D-4)' — hence 'D-2 plus half of D-15 disappear as a side effect' and 'that one move retires D-2, D-4, D-13, D-14, D-15 outright'.
killed.refutation: REFUTED TWICE OVER. (i) The producer's geometry does not clear the WCAG floor on a fine pointer. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/glass/glass-chip.css declares `.glass-chip__remove { display: inline-grid; flex: none; place-items: center; inline-size: 1.25rem; block-size: 1.25rem; … }` — 20 x 20 px. The 44 px seat (`inline-size: var(--touch-target, 2.75rem)`) lives ONLY inside `@media (pointer: coarse)`. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8's 24 x 24 floor is not pointer-conditional, so adopting Chip moves the desktop target 16 → 20 px and still fails. (ii) Worse, none of that stylesheet is in the served cascade in this consumer — see missed M1. So on this repo the cure would land a remove button with NO producer geometry on either pointer type. The defect D-15 names is real (confirmed, and raised to MAJOR); the prescribed cure does not close it, and the 'subtraction that dissolves five findings' framing at challenge-D-design.md:699-704 overstates what the transposition buys. (challenge-D-design.md:601-615, :186-188, :291-293)

killed.claim: 'No --animation-slide-sm/md/lg token and no producer spring is involved; 0.2s / cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) is the Tailwind default.'
killed.refutation: REFUTED. Tailwind v4's default transition duration is 150 ms, not 200 ms — so the measured 0.2s cannot be 'the Tailwind default'. It is the producer token, wired deliberately: glass-ui ships `--duration-fast: 0.2s`, sets `--default-transition-duration: var(--duration-fast, 150ms)` in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/components.css :root, and the demo re-affirms the binding by hand at demo/styles/foundation.css:128 — `--default-transition-duration: var(--duration-fast);`. The duration IS producer-tokenized and IS traceable to a named rung. Only the property-scope limb survives (transition-property: all at AdminTagsPanel.vue:99 sweeping the active:scale-95 transform and any property added later), and D itself correctly declines to file a PRM defect here — consistent with the two guards pinned at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md §1, which rewrite the property list to opacity/color/background-color/border-color/box-shadow under reduce. (challenge-D-design.md:582-597)

Badge's entire published surface is `variant | tone | size | surface | class` plus a default slot (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/badge/index.d.ts and Badge.vue.d.ts) — no interactive mode, no remove button, no emit. killed.claim: 'the port's published contract advertises a writable cell that throws "Write operation failed: computed value is readonly" at runtime'.

A setter-less computed's set path calls warn() and returns — the assignment is a silent no-op, and in a production build the warning branch is compiled out entirely, so a consumer writing groupedTags.value = x gets no signal at all. That is arguably worse than the filed claim, and it changes the remediation (the fix is the type declaration, not a try/catch), but the finding as written asserts a runtime behaviour the framework does not exhibit. killed.claim: 'if the admin toolbar genuinely needs a tighter rung than sm, that rung belongs in glass-ui as a size value; the six consumer sites then carry a prop, not a class.'

superlatives: The `error != empty` split is real, named, and rare. AdminTagsPanel.vue:67-79 renders a genuinely distinct error register, and the shared atom behind it is authored as TWO species with different roles and different content laws — demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:2-13 documents them (role="alert" at :17 for error vs role="status" at :28 for empty; the error variant DROPS the eyebrow and the ghost trio by the Q6 ruling). Most codebases collapse these three states into one plate. This one wrote down why it must not. All three axes conceded it (challenge-D-design.md:720-721).

EmptyState's `plate-ink` is a certified, floor-clamped ink rung with its provenance in the file. demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:49-54 and :95-104 name the measurement that motivated it (static text-muted-foreground composited 3.84:1 over the resting plate, under the 4.5:1 small-text floor), the cure (--ink-muted, boot-stamped and floor-clamped against the live resting plate), and the scope ('This is the ONE shared empty atom (8 consumers incl. the admin walls), so every consumer inherits the cure'). Exactly the discipline D-7 asks for; it exists and is simply not threaded at AdminTagsPanel.vue:87.

The producer's Chip is a genuinely well-built primitive and every criticism the corpus levels at the hand-rolled pill is something it already solved. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/chip/types.d.ts is a DISCRIMINATED prop union — modelValue?: never / removeLabel?: never on the non-applicable arms, so passing the wrong prop is a type error rather than a silent no-op — and removeLabel is REQUIRED on the removable arm, then additionally guarded at runtime by a watchEffect throwing TypeError("[Chip] mode=\"removable\" requires a non-empty removeLabel.") (dist/chip-DFZQr6rV.js). Its stylesheet ships a @media (pointer: coarse) block keeping a 20 px glyph inside a 44 px target and a prefers-reduced-motion carve-out zeroing --motion-weight. (That the stylesheet never reaches the page is a separate producer defect — missed M1 — not a design failing.)

Motion is governed centrally, demonstrably reaches this file, and both relevant axes checked it and RETRACTED their own first readings in writing. docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md §1 pins both guards with sha256 (demo/styles/animations.css:184-193 and glass-ui a11y-overrides.css:1) and measures that Guard 2 rewrites the transition PROPERTY LIST under reduce, deleting transform outright — so active:scale-95 at AdminTagsPanel.vue:99 never animates for a user who asked for less. D-14 files this as a tokenizing/property-scope issue and explicitly NOT a PRM defect (challenge-D-design.md:589-592); challenge-D-design.md:39-43 and challenge-C-implementation.md:457-459 each retract a first-pass 'keyboard focus is invisible' reading as a transition-timing artefact. Two independent seats publishing their own measurement errors is the strongest quality signal in this corpus.

The prior-art trail is honest, load-bearing, and predicted two of this component's live defects before this formation existed. docs/tranches/T/audit/w8-certification/passes/admin.p1.md row A-2 booked AdminTagsPanel.vue:87 (.section-label) at an analytic 3.72:1 and correctly graded itself ('proxy, light-only, de-emphasis — a flag for the census, not a certified fail'); row A-3 booked the loading-count lie, whose cure is visible in demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:119-128 for two of five routes. D-7 and C-8 each re-derive a row the ledger already carried, and both cite it.

The server side of the operation this UI mishandles is exemplary. api/src/modules/admin/service/tags.ts:69-90 wraps the delete + cascade in a single withTransaction and states the invariant in BOTH failure directions in prose at :76-82 — 'A partial failure must not leave a deleted tag whose name still appears in palettes[*].tags, nor a still-present tag whose name was already pulled from every palette' — with the post-txn emitAuditEvent deliberately outside the transaction. The route layer is equally disciplined: api/src/modules/admin/schema.ts:27-34 constrains name to min(1).max(30).regex(/^[a-z0-9-]+$/) before the service is reachable, which is what refutes D-10's rendering evidence outright.

superlatives: `demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:70` — `} satisfies Record<SpaceId, readonly ChannelMeta[]>` closes `PICKER_CHANNELS` over all 17 space ids at compile time. It is the reason the Components ROWS stay true even on the five cards where every other row is a lie (see the killed C-1 sub-claim). The correct discipline is already in the repo, ten lines from the table that lacks it — the D-1 repair is a copy, not an invention.

The published-surface boundary is right BY CONSTRUCTION, not by discipline. `grep -rn '@src|value\.js/src|\.\./\.\./\.\./src/' demo` returns nothing, and every one of the demo's five library specifiers (`/color`, `/css`, `/math`, `/easing`, `/quantize`) is a `package.json#exports` key. There is no demo import a real consumer could not write. L's negative proof at challenge-L-library.md:50-69 is the single most valuable page in the corpus and should survive any transposition verbatim.

`src/color/operations.ts:38` + `src/color/anchors.ts:368-377` — the library EMITS `"none"` for powerless hue (`oklch: c <= 0.000004`, `hwb: w + b >= 1`, `hsl: s*(1-|2l-1|) === 0`), and `numericSource` at `:17-24` re-admits hue-`none` as 0 while rejecting non-hue `none`. That is a precise, spec-faithful implementation of CSS Color 4 missing components, with the asymmetry in exactly the right place. The defect (L-2) is entirely on the demo's side of that boundary — the library is the party keeping its contract.

`src/color/operations.ts:229-238` — `clears` requires `Math.min(floatRatio, byteRatio) >= minimumRatio`, certifying against BOTH the continuous and the 8-bit-quantized ratio and taking the pessimistic one. Contrast solvers almost never do this; it is the difference between a ratio that survives rasterisation and one that does not. (It is also, ironically, what makes C-2's null arm reachable — a conservative primitive exposing a fail-open consumer.)

`demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:69-79, 93-118, 133-146` — the live tier-tint probe. Rather than certify ink against a token's nominal value, it stamps `var(--glass-bg-resting)` on a hidden in-cascade element, dual-ground-draws it through a 1x1 canvas to recover concrete sRGB AND alpha, memoizes the OKLab L, and gates the whole thing on a mount `probeEpoch` so a first read taken while the subtree is still detached cannot cache forever. The comment at `:60-67` records the exact regression that earned the epoch (3.59:1 measured against a modelled 0.90). This is instrumentation, not decoration, and it is why the D-11 mechanism limb had to be killed.

`ColorNutritionLabel.vue:190-208` — the D6 fg/bg double-duty split. Recognising that one guard call cannot certify a value used as BOTH foreground ink and background fill, splitting the roles, and deriving the fill's ink from the fill's own luminance (`contrastInkFor`) rather than reusing the foreground-certified value, is the right shape, and the comment records the measured 1.57:1 defect it cured. The `?? ""` at `:208` undoes part of it (C-2) — but the reasoning it interrupts is the best thinking in the file.

`demo/color-session/valueDomain.ts:1-49` — the dynamic-max write gate, whose header states the three per-channel semantics (linear clamps; hue WRAPS because `hsl(540 …)` IS `hsl(180 …)` per CSS; non-finite passes through) and then justifies why the demo owns the domain and the parser must not. `clampPickerColor` (`picker-color.ts:195-203`) implements exactly that, including preserving `"none"`. Correct CSS semantics AND a correct layering argument, in one 49-line module.
